note: Compassion & Choices argue AD laws IMPROVE end-of-life care, which is a direct counter to the proposition that better palliative care removes the case for AD. Direction right, passage on point.
Criticises the White Paper for removing competition safeguards — against reducing competition rules.
The GP argues demand will always outstrip supply and warns against widening ACCESS. Nothing about GP funding as a share of the NHS budget; a position was attached to a topically-adjacent passage.
FODO states in terms that zoning within facilities makes cross-contamination harder to control.
'schools ... receive few resources to do so' is an argument FOR adequate funding. Recorded as AGAINST.
Explicit: 'cannot condone or collaborate with any form of assisted suicide'. Capacity 'representative' is right — he writes as Chairman for the charity.
'PCNs would destroy continuity of care' is a DEFENCE of continuity. Recorded as AGAINST prioritising it.
Somerset LMC are sceptical of digital-first, not balanced on it; the passage is a warning, not a weighing.
'a great believer in continuity for a condition more than continuity per se ... a named GP is often a paper exercise' is genuinely balanced.
'Work for an NHS that recognises what we do' supports the profession but says nothing about media portrayal — half the proposition.
The BGS passage is about proactive case-finding for frail older people. The 10-minute consultation model is not addressed anywhere in it.
Postcode lottery → entrenched inequalities → 'nationally mandated measures'. Supports a cross-government approach.
Supports staff skills in general; silent on MANDATORY and on Initial Teacher Training, which is what the proposition specifies.
'An effective partnership has been with pharmacists' — thin but squarely supportive of integrating non-GP clinicians.
The passage is a premise about dignity being socially conferred. Living and Dying Well do hold the position, but this passage does not carry it.
'Social connection: age-friendly neighbourhoods' is a separate priority listed alongside activity, not a claim that activity interventions should include a social element.
RCS Edinburgh state the whole-system case explicitly and criticise individual-responsibility framing.
The passage is about the consequences of falls. No claim about a social element in activity interventions.
Care England's numbered recommendation list is exactly the proposition.
Argues for awareness campaigns about strength; does not argue for prioritising FUNDING for muscle-focused services.
Breast Cancer Now describe a backlog and ask for workforce modelling. They do not call for the NHS to publish a backlog assessment.
CSP: rehabilitation 'already overstretched ... not equipped to meet the needs'. Supports expansion.
Workload and under-resourcing. The 10-minute model is not mentioned.
'Removal of many indicators of QOF that have become ... a tick boxing exercise' is the claim.
'Investment in workforce capacity is critical to meeting current and future demand'.
'For us locally the Partnership model IS sustainable' — the proposition verbatim.
'Housing, employment, finances all are key and so requires a joined up multiagency approach'.

RCPCH describe their own data-collection project; that is adjacent to, not the same as, the NHS publishing a backlog assessment. ⚠ also an entity defect: the submitter is recorded as an individual while the document is RCPCH's.
Swim England argue swimming helps MSK conditions. The proposition is about embedding MSK prevention in the Major Conditions Strategy, which they do not address.
The passage is about pay, stress and recruitment. Bureaucracy is not its subject.
A warning about a surge in cancer diagnoses. No call for a published backlog assessment.
Social Work England describe what integration should achieve and their own role. They do not claim the White Paper WILL deliver it, which is the proposition.
A school's list of current practices ('regular referrals to CAMHS'). Nothing about extending services to a 0-25 range.
'The programme was co-designed with older adults and local community partners' — the proposition exactly.
'Integrated Multi-Agency Support ... to coordinate care, benefits, and housing'.
'Investment in transformation on a local level' with the funding gap spelled out.
Block contracts and work pushed beyond core hours. The 10-minute model is not the subject — the third of four positions on this proposition to fail the same way.
The Nuffield Trust passage is about matching care to patients and policy levers. Bureaucracy is not argued anywhere in it.
'Greater funding to recruit a range of co-workers ... working in an integrated and collaborative way would be desirable'.
Cornwall Mind propose crisis alternatives and first-responder programmes — improving access, but not the 'no wrong door' principle the proposition names.
Sportsgroup argue physical activity prevents disease. The proposition's specific content — embedding it in routine healthcare with clinicians equipped to advise — is absent.
'support schools deliver the kind of PHSE curriculum that students need and deserve' — directly on the proposition.

⚠ The 'passage' is a line from the BIBLIOGRAPHY — a cited paper's title. A reference list is not an argument, and the extract check cannot tell the difference because the words really are in the document.
'making sure they can effectively segregate COVID and non-COVID patients' as a challenge to be met.
'care coordination as a vital intervention ... long-term light touch monitoring ... to avoid harmful transitions'.
BACP recommend training be OFFERED, with refreshers. The proposition says mandatory and in Initial Teacher Training; neither is claimed.
Supports community-anchor delivery. Says nothing about peer-led, and asserts no effectiveness claim.
OHA warn that without action the medication becomes the preserve of private payers — an argument for NHS accessibility.
The passage is BAPO introducing itself ('our thoughts on this topic are vital'). A self-description is not a position on expanding rehabilitation.
A detailed list of bureaucracy reductions — CQC, QOF, unified record, Medical PAs, Fit Notes.
